label: NOTE: what this set reaches, and the one input that makes a store ORDER a claim
why: The nine members here are the phase 4 upstream generators and setMappingParams, read out of .text+0x17840-0x18054. Every entry is a claim the disassembly makes: which constant each scrambler call is fed, which bulk form (all-ones or all-zeros) each uses, where the differential bit is folded in, that generateCPt toggles below 25 symbols and scrambles from a base of 25 above it, that generateCPu and generateSUVu have IDENTICAL bodies and generateRm and generateB1u likewise, and that setMappingParams neither stores its argument nor does anything but reconfigure the chain. THE STORE ORDER ENTRIES ARE ONLY CATCHABLE AT bitsPerSymbol == 0, where `bits[-1]` is the top byte of prevBit and the two stores overlap; at every other input they are disjoint and finding 617's rule -- that a store order is a codegen hint the differential tier cannot settle -- applies unchanged. WHAT NO ENTRY HERE REACHES: which of generateCPu and generateSUVu is which, because their bodies are the same instructions in the same order and only `pattern`'s contents tell them apart.

label: NOTE: no entry here claims a store ORDER, and one used to
why: generateCPu and generateSUVu store the folded bit and then prevBit; generateE2u and generateTRN2u store prevBit and then the bit. Four mutations exchanged those orders and all four were caught -- under GCC 13, at bitsPerSymbol == 0, the only input where the two stores overlap because `bits[-1]` is prevBit's top byte. Under the PERIOD compiler the same trials fail on the unmutated source: 3.4.2 schedules the byte store first in E2u and TRN2u whatever the source says. The subscript is out of bounds and the behaviour is therefore the compiler's, not the object's, so the trials came out of the grid and these four claims came out of this set. Finding 4705, deviation D561. What still holds is everything the fold DOES: which bit it lands on, that prevBit carries it, and that both are written -- entries above cover all three.
